title: How good is Bo Nix compared to the other quarterbacks drafted in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft?
text:
The quarterback position is arguably not only the most important position in football, but the most important position in any major sport. Because of how important the quarterback is to an NFL team, there is heavy pressure on them to win games and play well.
Ever since Peyton Manning retired after the Broncos victory in Super Bowl 50, the Broncos have gone through 13 different quarterbacks (yes that includes Kendall Hinton who played quarterback after all of the quarterbacks got COVID) before drafting Bo Nix.
Coming out of college, many draft analysts questioned his age, the amount of short passes he’s thrown in Oregon and his upside. In a draft that was considered deep in the quarterback position, Bo Nix was the last quarterback taken in the first round when the Broncos drafted him with the 12th pick of the 2024 NFL Draft.
Like the other quarterbacks, Nix has been constantly compared to the other quarterbacks taken in the first round of the 2024 Draft. Caleb Williams, the first overall pick, has flashed his upside in his first year with Ben Johnson as head coach and is now on the Madden 27 cover, Jayden Daniels, the second overall pick, won Offensive Rookie of the Year and his rookie year is considered to be one of the greatest rookie seasons for a quarterback. However, a slight dop in play and injuries in his second year have made people question his longevity. The third overall pick, Drake Maye came second in MVP voting and made the Super Bowl in just his second year although fans point out his historically easy schedule and struggles in the postseason. The Falcons surprised the whole league when they made Michael Penix Jr. the eighth overall pick and the fourth quarterback taken after paying Kirk Cousins. However, inconsistent play in his sophomore season in the NFL led the Falcons to signing Tua Tagovailoa to compete with Penix and his future has been in question despite being the starter in 2026. J.J. McCarthy, the fifth quarterback taken and the tenth overall pick by the Vikings. missed his whole rookie season due to injury and struggled mightily in his first year as starter. He has since been traded to the New York Giants, hoping to revive his career after losing the starting job to Kyler Murray.
Since entering the NFL, Nix has been one of the most polarizing players. Critics point out how while his arm strength and athleticism is a lot better than they thought, he continues to frequently take checkdowns or short passes rather than being more aggressive and the Broncos offense has been inconsistent. Fans, however, point out his record breaking number of 4th quarter comebacks and his record.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggalt)
library(ggrepel)

nix <- read_csv("bo_nix.csv")
williams <- read_csv("caleb_williams.csv")
daniels <- read_csv("jayden_daniels.csv")
maye <- read_csv("drake_maye.csv")
penix <- read_csv("michael_penix.csv")
mccarthy <- read_csv("jj_mccarthy.csv")




Code
quarterbacks <- bind_rows(
  mutate(nix, player = "Bo Nix"),
  mutate(williams, player = "Caleb Williams"),
  mutate(daniels, player = "Jayden Daniels"),
  mutate(maye, player = "Drake Maye"),
  mutate(penix, player = "Michael Penix Jr."),
  mutate(mccarthy, player = "J.J. McCarthy")
)




Code
career <- quarterbacks |>
  group_by(player) |>
  summarize(
    games = sum(G, na.rm = TRUE),
    starts = sum(GS, na.rm = TRUE),
    touchdowns = sum(TD, na.rm = TRUE),
    interceptions = sum(Int, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    td_per_game = touchdowns / games,
    wins = case_when(
      player == "Bo Nix" ~ 30,
      player == "Caleb Williams" ~ 19,
      player == "Jayden Daniels" ~ 15,
      player == "Drake Maye" ~ 22,
      player == "J.J. McCarthy" ~ 7,
      player == "Michael Penix Jr." ~ 7
    ),
    losses = case_when(
      player == "Bo Nix" ~ 12,
      player == "Caleb Williams" ~ 19,
      player == "Jayden Daniels" ~ 13,
      player == "Drake Maye" ~ 15,
      player == "J.J. McCarthy" ~ 4,
      player == "Michael Penix Jr." ~ 11
    )
  )




Code
bo_nix <- career |>
  filter(player == "Bo Nix")




Code
ggplot() +
  geom_bar(
    data = career,
    aes(x = reorder(player, wins), weight = wins),
    fill = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  geom_bar(
    data = bo_nix,
    aes(x = reorder(player, wins), weight = wins),
    fill = "navy"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Bo Nix leads his draft class in wins",
    subtitle = "Quarterback wins from 2024 through the available 2026 games.",
    x = "",
    y = "Career wins",
    caption = "Source: Pro Football Reference | Graphic: Stephen Tran"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9)
  )









No matter how good or bad a quarterback plays, at the end of the day, the only result that matters is whether or not they won. Since entering the NFL, all Bo Nix knows has been winning. From 2024 to week 8 of the 2026 season, Bo Nix has lead the quarterbacks in his draft class with 30 wins and 12 losses. That is 8 more than Drake Maye who has 22. Caleb Williams has a total of 19 wins, Jayden Daniels has 15 wins while Michael Penix and J.J. McCarthy only have 7.
However, this does not tell the whole story. Despite having more wins than his draft mates, Bo Nix has been the only quarterback out of these 6 to have played every single game since week 1 of his rookie season. Maye, Penix and McCarthy did not start immediately their rookie year (and as mentioned earlier, McCarthy missed his whole rookie year due to injury) while Jayden Daniels missed a large chunk of his sophomore season while Caleb WIlliams missed a few games so far in 2026.
However, if we break it down to win percentage, Nix leads all of his peers with a win rate of 71.4%. Drake Maye, the closest quarterback in terms of total wins compared to Nix has only won about 59.5% of his starts, a steep drop off.
Critics point out that despite Bo Nix’s historic success to start his career, his offenses have been inconsistent and mediocre. Critics instead point out to the talent on the roster that contributed to Bo Nix’s wins and that the Broncos defense has bailed out Nix several times in his career. However, fans point out that Nix is one of, if not the clutchest quarterback in the NFL with all of his 4th quarter comebacks.


Code
ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = career,
    aes(x = touchdowns, y = interceptions),
    color = "darkgrey",
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = bo_nix,
    aes(x = touchdowns, y = interceptions),
    color = "navy",
    size = 5
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = career,
    aes(
      x = touchdowns,
      y = interceptions,
      label = player
    ),
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bo Nix leads in touchdowns thrown but also leads\nin interceptions thrown",
    subtitle = "Career passing touchdowns compared with interceptions for the six first round quarterbacks in 2024.",
    x = "Career passing touchdowns",
    y = "Career interceptions",
    caption = "Source: Pro Football Reference | Graphic: Stephen Tran"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9)
  )









When you look at the box score of a quarterback, most people immediately look at the amount of touchdowns and interceptions thrown. Nix leads the 2024 quarterback class with 63 career touchdown passes. Maye is slightly behind him with 61 touchdown passes. Caleb Williams is in third with 52 touchdown passes, Daniels has 39, Penix has 21 while McCarthy only has 12.
However, while Nix and Maye have led the class in touchdown passes, they both are tied with the most interceptions thrown with 26. Caleb Williams on the other hand has thrown only 14 interceptions. This raises questions about how much Nix’s total production reflects his ability and decision making compared to his playing time. Like his win total, Nix has had more opportunities to throw more touchdowns and interceptions because he has played more games than the other quarterbacks.
Williams is the most interesting comparison to Nix. Although Williams has thrown 11 fewer touchdowns than Nix, he has also thrown 12 fewer interceptions. This suggests that Williams is better at protecting the football while producing touchdowns.


Code
ggplot() +
  geom_bar(
    data = career,
    aes(x = reorder(player, td_per_game), weight = td_per_game),
    fill = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  geom_bar(
    data = bo_nix,
    aes(x = reorder(player, td_per_game), weight = td_per_game),
    fill = "navy"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Drake Maye edges out Bo Nix in touchdowns per game",
    subtitle = "Passing touchdowns per game from 2024 through the available 2026 games.",
    x = "",
    y = "Passing touchdowns per game",
    caption = "Source: Pro Football Reference | Graphic: Stephen Tran"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9)
  )









Because the 6 other quarterbacks have played different amounts of games compared to each other, a great way of showing off their production is the amount of touchdown passes each quarterback averages per game.
This is where Drake Maye takes the lead. Maye has averaged about 1.61 passing touchdowns per game since entering the league. This is slightly ahead of Nix who has averaged with 1.5 touchdowns per game. Williams is in third with 1.37 and Daniels has 1.34. Penix only averages 1.05 touchdowns per game while J.J. McCarthy averages 0.92 touchdowns a game which means he averages less than a single passing touchdown per game.
Maye stands out even more when you take into account that he did not begin his rookie season as the starting quarterback for the Patriots which means he has played fewer games than NIx but nearly matched his total passing touchdowns. However, the difference between both quarterbacks is relatively small.
So, has Bo Nix been the most successful quarterback taken in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft?
If success is based on winning games, Nix has by far the strongest argument. Even though being the last quarterback taken in the first round, he has recorded more wins than any off his classmates and leads them all with passing touchdowns.
However, Maye has averaged more passing touchdowns per game and it is clear that Williams has been the best at limiting turnovers while still finding ways to score through the air.
It is also important to take note that Nix has benefited from starting more games than the other quarterbacks. As the old saying goes, the best ability is availability and Nix has played every regular season game for the Broncos since day 1.
In conclusion, it is difficult to evaluate whether or not Nix is the most successful quarterback from his draft class so far, especially with players like Maye and Williams putting up impressive numbers and Jayden Daniels having the opportunity to flash his upside since his incredible rookie year. However, it is clear that Nix has been unfairly criticized, especially when the numbers are a lot closer than it appears.
